tagline: From Brownsville up the South Santiam to Tombstone Pass.
intro: Out of the valley farmland at Brownsville the byway runs east past Crawfordsville and Holley to Sweet Home, then follows US 20 and the South Santiam River up into thick forest. Past Mountain House the road leaves the river and climbs toward Tombstone Pass, 4,241 feet, gaining more than 2,500 feet in seven miles. Near the end an old-growth trail passes trees more than 500 years old.

Much of the way keeps to the line of the Santiam Wagon Road, a toll road built to take settlers out of the valley to the pastures of central Oregon. In 1905 the first transcontinental auto race came over it, and the winner reached Portland from New York in 40 days.
season: TripCheck lists it as a year-round drive.

moments.title: Brownsville
moments.text: Rob Reiner filmed Stand by Me here in the summer of 1985 with about 100 locals as extras, and since 2007 the town has held a Stand by Me Day.

moments.title: Crawfordsville Bridge
moments.text: The 1932 covered bridge beside the highway was bypassed in 1963 and now carries only walkers over the Calapooia River.

moments.title: Cascadia
moments.text: First a stage stop on the wagon road, then a resort selling the curative powers of Soda Creek's mineral water, Cascadia still shows old wagon ruts where the creek meets the river.
